chapters.title: Lanes
chapters.source: ASAM OpenDRIVE 1.7.0 ch.9 (local HTML), cross-checked with 1.9.0 ch.11 online and OpenDRIVE 1.8.1 XSD (tests/xsd/opendrive_1_8_1); figures in C:/mywork/osm2carla/build/tmp/specfig/ch9/

sections.title: Lanes (introduction, ids, center lane)
sections.summary: Every road carries lanes inside <lanes>. A zero-width center lane with id 0 is the numbering reference: ids ascend to the left (+t) and descend to the right (-t). Without a laneOffset the center lane coincides with the road reference line; on two-way roads it usually separates the driving directions, on one-way roads all lanes may sit on one side.
concepts: center lane: id 0, no width, carries the center roadMark; it is the t-origin of the lane stack after laneOffset is applied
left lanes: ids 1,2,3... outward in +t; right lanes: ids -1,-2,-3... outward in -t
driving direction is derived from id sign and road rule (RHT: right lanes drive with s, left lanes against s; LHT reversed)
minimum road (1.7): center lane plus one lane with width > 0; 1.9 relaxes this (roads used as junction boundaries may have no width>0 lane)
number of lanes is unlimited
<lanes> contains: laneOffset*, laneSection+ (1.9: <lanes> may be repeated with @layer permanent|temporary)

formulas.name: lane direction from id
formulas.expr: RHT: id<0 -> travels +s, id>0 -> travels -s; LHT: inverse

rules.text: Each road has a center lane and at least one lane with width > 0 (1.9 rephrases to: at least one lane layer with a center lane; width>0 requirement dropped).
Each road has at least one lane layer with a center lane.
Roads may have as many lanes as needed.
Center lane has no width; never put <width> (or <border>) on lane 0.
Center lane id is 0.
Numbering starts at 1 / -1 next to the center lane; descends toward -t, ascends toward +t.
Lane ids are consecutive with no gaps (e.g. -1,-2,-3, never -1,-3).
Lane ids are unique per lane section (1.9: per section and layer).
Bidirectional lanes may exist (1.7: @type=bidirectional; 1.8+: @direction=both).
<lanes> contains at least one <laneSection>.
Every <laneSection> carries @s.
The first laneSection has s=0.0.
1.9 intro: all drivable lanes are continuous and smooth without gaps, considering plan view, profiles and lane properties (see Annex D).

use_cases.how: center lane on the reference line; RHT: forward lanes are -1..-n, backward lanes 1..m
put all traffic lanes on one side (right side for RHT, ids -1..-n); left side may be empty or hold only non-driving lanes; or use @direction (1.8+)

right: <center><lane id="0" type="none"><roadMark .../></lane></center> with no width child
ids -1,-2,-3 contiguous, listed in XML left to right (descending id: 2,1 | 0 | -1,-2)
wrong: id gaps after removing a lane (renumber instead)
assuming center lane == reference line when laneOffset != 0
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.8: <lane> on left/right gets @direction (standard|reversed|both), @advisory (none|inner|outer|both), @dynamicLaneDirection, @dynamicLaneType, @roadWorks; center lane @type and @level deprecated
1.9: lane layers (<lanes layer=permanent|temporary>), id uniqueness per layer, width>0 minimum requirement removed
figures: Figure 52 (img001): two-way road, center lane = reference line separates directions; lanes 3,2,1 | 0 | -1,-2, a right lane -3 appears via widening; lesson: ids are positional from center, new outer lane gets next id
Figure 53 (img002): one-way road, all lanes on one side of the center lane
Figure 54 (img003): UML of <lanes>

sections.title: Lane grouping within lane sections (left/center/right)
sections.summary: Within a laneSection lanes are grouped into <left>, <center>, <right>. Positive ids live in <left>, negative in <right>, id 0 in <center>. The group defines the side and (via the id sign) the default driving direction.
concepts: <left> lane id type positiveInteger, <right> negativeInteger, <center> integer (0)
a lane group = all lanes of one side; width vs border exclusivity and border 'inner lane' semantics are per group
XML order should be descending id within each group

attributes.name: type
attributes.meaning: deprecated in 1.8 for center lane; 1.7 writers normally put type="none"

attributes.name: level
attributes.meaning: true = exclude from superelevation/shape; default false

attributes.name: advisory
attributes.meaning: 1.8+: none|inner|outer|both; lane may be used by neighbouring traffic (e.g. advisory bike lane)

rules.text: Positive ids are left of the center lane, negative ids right.
Each laneSection contains at least one <left> or <right> (1.9: valid for the whole section length).
Exactly one <center> per s-coordinate (with singleSide sections, the center may live in only one of overlapping sections).
Each laneSection may contain one <center> (1.7 wording, to allow singleSide sections; element descriptions say one center shall exist per section).
List lanes left to right, i.e. descending id.
1.8+: @direction=reversed must not be used to switch the whole road between RHT and LHT (use road @rule).

use_cases.how: from id sign + road rule, unless type=bidirectional (1.7) / direction=both|reversed (1.8+)

right: <left> lanes 2 then 1, <center> 0, <right> -1 then -2
figures: Figure 55 (img004): left/center/right grouping of lanes

sections.title: Lane sections
sections.summary: A laneSection is an s-interval with a fixed set of lanes; a new section is required whenever the number of lanes changes. Sections are ascending in s, start at 0, have positive length and remain valid until the next one. @singleSide lets one side be split independently of the other.
concepts: section length is implicit: next section s (or road length) minus this s
lane properties (width, marks, speed...) may change freely inside a section; only lane count/set (and type) forces a new section
lane type changes need a new section (type is a lane attribute, not an s-dependent child)
singleSide=true: section applies to one side only, determined by its child groups (Figure 57)
an appearing/disappearing lane is modelled with width polynomial going from/to 0 inside a section, plus a section boundary where the count changes

attributes.name: s
attributes.meaning: start s of the section on the reference line

attributes.name: singleSide
attributes.meaning: section valid for one side only (left, center or right) depending on children

attributes.name: length
attributes.meaning: 1.9 only: explicit length, temporary layer only

formulas.name: section extent
formulas.expr: s in [s_i, s_{i+1}) ; last section ends at road @length

rules.text: Each road has at least one lane section.
laneSections ascending in s.
Section length > 0 (distance between consecutive sections not zero).
Exactly one center lane at each s-position.
Avoid zero-width lanes over long distances.
New lane section each time the number of lanes changes.
A lane section stays valid until the next one is defined (or road end).
Lane properties inside a section may change as often as needed.
Sections may be defined for one side only via @singleSide.
1.9: @length only on temporary-layer sections.
1.9: @length must not run past road end.
1.9: new permanent section wherever permanent lanes link to temporary lanes.

use_cases.how: section A: lanes -1,-2; section B starts where widening begins: lanes -1,-2,-3 where the new lane has width a=0 and cubic b,c,d grows it; link only continuing lanes

use_cases.case: lanes change at different s on each side (Figure 57)
use_cases.how: either split both sides at every change (simplest, always valid), or use singleSide sections
new section at the change s; link old lane to new lane

right: split at each lane-count change; copy unchanged lanes into the new section with links both ways
keep sections a few metres long at least (avoid micro sections)
wrong: changing lane count via width=0 without a section split
long stretches of width-0 lanes kept only to avoid splitting
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.9: @length (temporary layer only), permanent layer must cover road with no gaps, new rules lanesec_length_limit_road, new_lanesec_link_temp_to_perm
figures: Figure 56 (img005): section A has -1,-2; in section B a new outer lane grows and ids become -1,-2,-3 (new -2 grows between, old -2 becomes -3); lesson: when a lane appears, outer lanes get renumbered and a new section starts at the begin of the widening
Figure 57 (img006): left side and right side split at different s with singleSide sections

sections.title: Lane offset
sections.summary: <laneOffset> shifts the center lane laterally from the reference line by a cubic polynomial in s. It is typically used for local shifts such as left-turn pockets, so the reference line can stay smooth. Each element starts at absolute s and is valid until the next one; it is defined per road, not per section.
concepts: laneOffset is a child of <lanes>, independent of laneSection boundaries
positive offset moves the whole lane stack to +t (left)
default offset is 0 where no laneOffset is defined (before the first element)
lane borders t-positions = laneOffset + cumulative widths
linear interpolation recommended when combined with road shape (1.7) because shape uses linear interpolation

formulas.name: lane offset
formulas.expr: offset(ds) = a + b*ds + c*ds^2 + d*ds^3 ; ds = s - s_start
formulas.vars: s_start = laneOffset@s (absolute, NOT relative to laneSection)
formulas.notes: ds restarts at 0 for each element; new element whenever polynomial changes

formulas.name: t of lane borders (width mode)
formulas.expr: t_outer(i) = offset(s) + sign(i) * sum_{k=1..|i|} width_k(s) ; t_inner(i) = t_outer(i - sign(i)) ; t_outer(0)=offset(s)
formulas.vars: width_k evaluated with ds relative to section start + sOffset of the active width record
formulas.notes: left lanes sign=+1, right lanes sign=-1; center of lane i at (t_inner+t_outer)/2

formulas.name: smooth cubic transition of offset from 0 to D over L
formulas.vars: D target offset, L transition length
formulas.notes: C1 at both ends (slope 0); example Ex_Simple-LaneOffset: c=3.9e-3, d=-5.2e-5 over 50 m to 3.25 m

rules.text: 1.7: laneOffset shall not be used together with road shapes (rule dropped in 1.9 text; guidance remains to use linear interpolation for consistency).
laneOffset elements ascending in s.
Start a new laneOffset element when the polynomial changes.
No laneOffset if any <border> definitions exist on the road.
Use linear interpolation for offset when combined with shape.

use_cases.how: laneOffset ramps the center lane to +D while a new lane -1 grows from width 0 at the center; outer lanes renumber in new sections

use_cases.case: asymmetric road from OSM (more lanes one way)
use_cases.how: keep reference line on the OSM way and use laneOffset = (w_left - w_right)/2 or put reference on the separation line

right: cubic with zero slope at ends for transitions
evaluate offset with absolute s
wrong: offset s treated as relative to laneSection
step change in offset between elements (creates gap - violates Annex D)
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.9: each lane layer has its own laneOffset (temporary need not match permanent)
1.9 text drops the 1.7 'not with road shapes' shall-rule
figures: Figure 58 (img007): sections A-B-C, center lane offset from reference line via cubic; a lane appears at the center (new -1) and ids shift; lesson: offset moves the whole stack and lane appearance still needs sections+renumbering

sections.title: Lane linkage
sections.summary: Each lane can list <predecessor>/<successor> lane ids inside <link>. Predecessor = lane at the start of its section, successor = lane at the end, both in reference-line direction and independent of driving direction. Within a road the ids refer to the neighbouring section; across roads to the first/last section of the other road according to the road link contact point.
concepts: link direction is geometric (s), not traffic direction
across roads with contactPoint=end, ids may flip sign (Figure 59: road 10 lane -1 -> road 20 lane 1 because road 20 runs opposite)
links only where both lanes have non-zero width at the touch point and are semantically connected
multiple predecessors/successors for abrupt split/merge with non-zero width
appearing lane (width 0 at start) gets no predecessor; vanishing lane (width 0 at end) no successor
lanes into a junction: no lane link on the road side; connections are in junction <laneLink>

formulas.name: cross-road id mapping
formulas.expr: if road links contact the other road at its start and both run same way: same id; if contact at other road's end (opposite direction): id_other = -id typically
formulas.notes: not a spec formula; derived from Figure 59/Table 27

rules.text: A lane may have another lane as predecessor or successor.
Link only if physical connection exists at both lanes' ends, both non-zero width there, semantically connected.
Link only when the relationship is clear; if ambiguous use a junction.
Use multiple predecessors/successors for abrupt split/merge; all connected lanes non-zero width at the connection.
Lane with width 0 at section start has no <predecessor>.
Lane with width 0 at section end has no <successor>.
Omit <link> if the lane starts/ends in a junction or has no link.
A lane continuing across sections is linked in both directions.
When a new lane appears beside, link only the continuing lane to the original, not the appearing lane (no multiple successors).
1.9: at start/end of a temporary layer section all drivable non-zero-width temporary lanes link to permanent lanes.

use_cases.how: pred/succ both ways
link exit lane to offRamp lane (type change)

use_cases.case: roadside parking lane ends and the road continues
use_cases.how: parking lane successor = driving lane (vehicles continue)

use_cases.case: parking lane ends into grass strip
use_cases.how: no link

use_cases.case: bikeway ends, bikes continue on driving lane (Figure 60)
use_cases.how: bike lane successor = driving lane; driving lane has multiple predecessors

use_cases.case: abrupt split of one lane into two (Figure 61)
use_cases.how: one lane with two successors, both non-zero width
new lane: no predecessor; continuing lane links 1:1

right: symmetric links (A succ B <=> B pred A)
check width>0 at both ends before linking
use junction when mapping is ambiguous
wrong: appearing lane as second successor of the original
lane links on road ends that enter a junction
assuming successor = downstream in traffic direction
figures: Figure 59 (img008): roads 30-10-20; road 20 reversed so road10 lane -1 succ = road20 lane 1, lane 1 succ = road20 lane -1; lesson: sign flips when contactPoint=end
Figure 60 (img009): bike lane ends into driving lane (multiple links)
Figure 61 (img010): driving lane abruptly splits into two (multiple successors)
Figure 62 (img011): UML of link

sections.title: Lane properties (general)
sections.summary: Lane properties (width, border, material, speed, access, height, rule, roadMark) are children of <lane> with sOffset relative to the laneSection start. Each stays valid until the next element of the same kind or the section end, and same-kind elements are ascending. Applications may apply defaults where nothing is specified.
concepts: s_abs = laneSection@s + sOffset
properties do not carry over to the next laneSection: repeat them
same-kind elements may not be out of order

formulas.name: absolute s of a property
formulas.expr: s = s_section + sOffset (+ ds inside polynomial elements)
formulas.notes: applies to width, border, roadMark, material, speed, access, height, rule

rules.text: Properties defined relative to the start of their lane section.
A property stays valid until another of the same type is defined or the section ends.
Same-type properties in ascending order.

right: re-emit speed/roadMark/material in every section
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.9 splits into 11.7 lane geometry (width/border/height/level) and 11.8 lane properties (type/material/speed/access)
figures: Figure 63 (img012): UML of lane properties

sections.title: Lane width
sections.summary: <width> gives lane width as a cubic in ds measured from section start + sOffset, along the reference line (width is measured in t, perpendicular to the reference line, not to the lane). A width record must exist at sOffset=0 and widths must be >= 0. Width and border are mutually exclusive per lane group; if both exist, width wins.
concepts: width is along t at a given s (perpendicular to reference line)
appearing lane: a=0 and growing cubic; disappearing: cubic falling to 0 at section end
if both width and border present, application must use width

formulas.name: lane width
formulas.notes: ds restarts at 0 for each width element

formulas.name: smooth taper 0 -> W over L
formulas.vars: W final width, L taper length
formulas.notes: C1, monotone; reverse (W -> 0): a=W, b=0, c=-3W/L^2, d=2W/L^3

rules.text: Width defined at least once per lane section.
Width covers the full section: a <width> with sOffset=0 must exist.
No <width> on the center lane.
Width valid until next width element or section end.
New width element when the polynomial changes.
Width not combined with border in the same lane group.
<width> ascending in sOffset.
width(ds) >= 0 everywhere.

use_cases.how: new section B; lane -2 has a=0 and b,c,d widening; lane -1 constant

right: first width sOffset=0
check cubic stays >=0 across its interval (cubic can dip negative)
continuous width between consecutive width records and across sections for continuing lanes
wrong: width jumps across section boundary for the same physical lane (gap, Annex D)
figures: Figure 64 (img013): ds restarts per section; lane -1 constant a in section A, new lane -2 starts with a=0 and widens in section B

sections.title: Lane borders
sections.summary: <border> alternatively gives the t-position of a lane's outer edge as a cubic in ds, independent of inner lanes (same sign, smaller |id|). Meant for measured data to avoid many sections. Exclusive with width in a lane group and with laneOffset; borders must not cross inner lanes.
concepts: border value is a t-coordinate of the outer edge measured from the reference line (signed; right-side borders are negative in strict reading; some tools interpret differently)
inner edge of lane i = outer edge of lane i-sign(i) (or center lane)
no laneOffset allowed, so center lane = reference line

rules.text: No width together with border in the same lane group.
No border together with laneOffset.
New border element when polynomial changes.
<border> ascending.
Borders do not intersect inner lanes.
If both width and border exist, applications use width.

use_cases.how: fit border cubic per lane outer edge

right: prefer <width> for generated data (OdrForge): wider tool support
wrong: mixing width and border in one group
figures: Figure 65 (img014): a_lane-2 = a_lane-1 at start (zero width), lane -2 border widens; lesson: border coordinates are absolute t-positions, independent of inner lanes

sections.title: Lane type and lane element attributes
sections.summary: @type states the main purpose and traffic rules of a lane. The 1.7 enum e_laneType has 28 values; 1.8 added shared, walking and slipLane and deprecated several (sidewalk, bidirectional, bus, taxi, HOV, special1-3, roadWorks, mwyEntry, mwyExit). A type change requires a new lane section.
concepts: lane types (1.7 enum): shoulder, border, driving, stop, none, restricted, parking, median, biking, sidewalk, curb, exit, entry, onRamp, offRamp, connectingRamp, bidirectional, special1, special2, special3, roadWorks, tram, rail, bus, taxi, HOV, mwyEntry, mwyExit
shoulder: soft border at road edge (grass/gravel), not normally driven [since 1.4; non-drivable]
border: hard border at road edge, same height as driving lane [since 1.4; drivable in Annex D list]
driving: normal drivable lane not covered by other types [since 1.4; drivable]
stop: motorway hard shoulder for emergency stops [since 1.4; drivable]
none: outermost space with no content; lets apps know OpenDRIVE still exists if driver leaves road [since 1.4; non-drivable]
restricted: same height as driving lanes, cars should not drive (hatched/blocked area) [since 1.4; drivable in Annex D]
parking: lane with parking spaces [since 1.4; not in drivable list]
median: between opposite-direction driving lanes (central reservation) [since 1.4; non-drivable]
biking: reserved for cyclists [since 1.4; drivable only if advisory (Annex D)]
sidewalk: pedestrian walkway; deprecated in 1.8, use walking [since 1.4; non-drivable]
curb: curb stones, different height than adjacent drivable lane (use with <height>) [since 1.4; non-drivable]
exit: parallel to main road, leads off (deceleration lane) [since 1.4; drivable]
entry: parallel to main road, merges in (acceleration lane) [since 1.4; drivable]
onRamp: ramp to motorway from rural/urban roads (1.7 text spells 'onramp'; enum value onRamp) [since 1.4; drivable]
offRamp: ramp from motorway to rural/urban roads [since 1.4; drivable]
connectingRamp: ramp connecting two motorways (motorway interchange) [since 1.4; drivable]
bidirectional: lane usable in both directions (center turn lane etc.); deprecated in 1.8, use @direction=both [since 1.4; drivable (deprecated)]
special1: application-specific; deprecated 1.8 [since 1.4]
special2: application-specific; deprecated 1.8 [since 1.4]
special3: application-specific; deprecated 1.8 [since 1.4]
roadWorks: lane under construction; deprecated 1.8, use @roadWorks=true (+ 1.9 temporary layer) [since 1.4; deprecated]
tram: used by trams only [since 1.4]
rail: used by trains only [since 1.4]
bus: bus lane; deprecated 1.8, use type=driving + <access><restriction type=bus> [since 1.4; deprecated drivable]
taxi: taxi lane; deprecated 1.8, use <access> [since 1.4; deprecated drivable]
HOV: high-occupancy/carpool lane; deprecated 1.8, use <access> (restriction HOV) [since 1.4; deprecated drivable]
mwyEntry: motorway entry; deprecated (use entry) [since 1.4; deprecated]
mwyExit: motorway exit; deprecated (use exit) [since 1.4; deprecated]
shared: 1.8: shared by all participants; for walking/biking sharing use <access> [since 1.8]
walking: 1.8: pedestrian lane (replaces sidewalk) [since 1.8; non-drivable]
slipLane: 1.8: lets drivers change roads without entering the main intersection (free right turn) [since 1.8; drivable]

Annex D (1.9) drivable types: driving, entry, exit, onRamp, offRamp, connectingRamp, slipLane, biking (advisory only), border, stop, restricted; deprecated drivable: HOV, bidirectional, bus, mwyEntry, mwyExit, roadWorks, taxi
CARLA/RoadRunner practice: driving lanes must be type driving to be routable; sidewalk(1.7)/walking for pedestrians

attributes.name: level
attributes.meaning: true: keep level (no superelevation/shape); false default

rules.text: Lane type may change as often as needed, but only via a new lane section.

use_cases.how: shoulder | border | driving x3 | stop | shoulder | none
driving lanes with shoulder/border edges, optional median
border/curb | driving x2 | curb median curb | driving x2 | border | curb | parking | shoulder | biking | sidewalk
exit lane parallel to main road -> offRamp; onRamp -> entry lane parallel, merging
connectingRamp
sidewalk (1.7) or walking (1.8+), with curb lane or <height>
1.7: type bus; 1.8+: driving + access restriction bus

right: write enum spelling exactly (onRamp, offRamp, connectingRamp, HOV)
target-version-aware: sidewalk in 1.7, walking in 1.8+
wrong: using bidirectional in 1.8+ output instead of @direction=both
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.8 deprecated: sidewalk(->walking), bidirectional(->@direction), bus/taxi/HOV(->access), special1-3, roadWorks(->@roadWorks), mwyEntry/mwyExit (->entry/exit)
figures: Figures 66-70 (img015-img019): lane-type layouts for motorway, rural, urban, exit/entry and motorway-to-motorway; lesson: shoulder/border/none at edges, stop = hard shoulder, curb + median separate opposing urban carriageways, exit->offRamp and onRamp->entry transitions

sections.title: Lane material
sections.summary: <material> stores surface code, friction and roughness for a lane from sOffset on. Valid until the next material or section end; not on the center lane. Defaults are application-defined.
concepts: complements OpenCRG
surface is an application-specific code

rules.text: No material on center lane.
Material valid until next material or section end.
Ascending order.

use_cases.how: map to surface string + typical friction

sections.title: Lane speed limit
sections.summary: <speed> sets a lane's maximum speed from sOffset; it overrides the road-level speed but signals take precedence. Unit defaults to m/s.
concepts: precedence: signals > lane <speed> > road <type><speed>
e_unitSpeed: m/s, km/h, mph

rules.text: No speed on center lane.
Valid until next speed or section end.
Ascending order.
Signal-derived limits always take preference.

use_cases.how: per-lane <speed unit=km/h>

right: always give unit explicitly
wrong: max=50 without unit meaning km/h (it is m/s!)
figures: Figure 71 (img020): lane-specific speed limits

sections.title: Lane access
sections.summary: <access> restricts lanes to or from road-user classes, in addition to signals. 'allow' lists the only permitted users; 'deny' bans the listed users and keeps all others; allow and deny may not be mixed at the same s. At every new s all restrictions must be restated; deny + none clears previous restrictions.
concepts: e_accessRestrictionType (1.7): simulator, autonomousTraffic, pedestrian, passengerCar, bus, delivery, emergency, taxi, throughTraffic, truck, bicycle, motorcycle, none, trucks; 1.8 adds HOV
rule enum: allow | deny
several <access> at the same sOffset form the restriction set at that s
no <access> = unrestricted

attributes.name: rule
attributes.meaning: allow = only listed may use; deny = listed banned

attributes.name: restriction
attributes.meaning: 1.7: participant class; deprecated in 1.8 in favour of child <restriction>

rules.text: No access on center lane.
Valid until next access or section end.
Ascending order.
Access elements may start at identical sOffset.
No access element = no restrictions.
deny: listed denied, all others allowed.
allow: listed allowed, all others banned.
At a given s, only allow or only deny, never mixed.
At each new s-position restate all restrictions even if only a subset changes.
deny with restriction none reverts all previous restrictions.

use_cases.how: 1.7: <access sOffset=0 rule=allow restriction=bus/> (+ taxi etc. as more elements at same sOffset); 1.8+: <access sOffset=0 rule=allow><restriction type=bus/></access>
rule=deny restriction=truck
new access at sOffset with rule=deny restriction=none

right: restate full set at each sOffset
wrong: allow bus + deny truck at same s
assuming restrictions persist into next laneSection
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.8: @restriction deprecated, child <restriction type> added; HOV value added
figures: Figure 72 (img021): bus lane via access

sections.title: Lane height
sections.summary: <height> raises a lane's inner and outer edge by small offsets in h (z) above the road surface (which already includes elevation, superelevation and shape). Used for curbs and raised sidewalks, never for road elevation.
concepts: inner = edge toward center lane, outer = away from it
value is constant from sOffset until next height (no polynomial); across the lane, linear between inner and outer (interpretation)
center lane cannot be raised

attributes.name: inner
attributes.meaning: offset at inner edge from road level

attributes.name: outer
attributes.meaning: offset at outer edge from road level

formulas.name: lane surface height
formulas.notes: linear lateral interpolation is the common reading; spec gives only inner/outer values; step change at each new <height>

rules.text: Use <height> to modify lane height (e.g. curbstones).
Ascending order.
Center lane not elevated by height.
Not used for road elevation/superelevation.
Only small-scale elevation.

use_cases.how: <height sOffset=0 inner=0.12 outer=0.12/> on sidewalk lane; curb lane inner 0 -> outer 0.12 or step

changes_1_8_1_9: 1.9 text: offset is in h-direction relative to road incl. crossSectionSurface (1.8 lateral profile surface)
figures: Figure 73 (img022): sidewalk raised by lane height over the superelevated road

sections.title: Excluding lanes from superelevation (@level)
sections.summary: level=true excludes a lane from superelevation and road shape; it stays flat at the height of the adjacent inner lane's outer edge. If a lane is level, all lanes outward of it on that side must also be level.
concepts: typical: curbs, borders, sidewalks on banked roads
level lanes continue horizontally from the inner neighbour's outer edge

formulas.name: level lane z
formulas.expr: z(s,t) = z_road(s, t_inner_edge) for all t in lane

rules.text: If a lane has level=true, all lanes from it to the road edge (on at least one side) are level=true.
Multiple outer lanes may have level=true (e.g. bike lane + sidewalk).
1.9: avoid changing @level between lane sections.

use_cases.how: sidewalk and curb level=true

wrong: level=true on an inner lane with non-level lane outside it
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.8/1.9: level also excludes crossSectionSurface; center lane @level deprecated

sections.title: Road markings (<roadMark>)
sections.summary: <roadMark> describes the line at a lane's outer border (left border for left lanes, right border for right lanes); the center lane's roadMark is the dividing line. The mark is centered on that border so half of it lies on the next lane outward. Simple style via @type keyword, detailed via <type>/<line> (repeating) or <explicit> (non-repeating), with optional <sway>.
concepts: roadMark types (e_roadMarkType): none: no marking; solid: single continuous line; broken: single dashed line; solid solid: double continuous; solid broken: double line, one solid one broken; spec does not define which side is which - tools differ, so set laneChange explicitly; broken solid: double line, broken + solid (mirror of solid broken; side order not defined in spec); broken broken: double dashed; botts dots: raised pavement markers; grass: grass edge, no paint; curb: curb edge; custom: use <type>/<line> detail; edge: edge of road surface (no paint)
colors (e_roadMarkColor 1.7): standard (application default, usually white), blue, green, orange, red, violet, white, yellow; 1.8 adds black
weights (e_roadMarkWeight): standard, bold (common convention: standard 0.12 m, bold 0.25 m width; not normative in 1.7)

laneChange (e_road_lanes_laneSection_lcr_lane_roadMark_laneChange): increase = crossing allowed toward increasing lane id, decrease = toward decreasing id, both (default if missing), none = no crossing; ids increase right-to-left in s direction
line @rule (e_roadMarkRule): no passing, caution, none; applies when crossing from inside (lower |id|) to outside (higher |id|)
multiple roadMarks per lane, ascending sOffset, each valid until next or section end
for the outermost lane, its roadMark is the road edge line
1.9: stop lines and other guidance markings -> signals (+objects); non-mandatory markings -> objects

attributes.name: width
attributes.meaning: line width; optional when <line> detail given

formulas.name: roadMark lateral position
formulas.expr: t_mark_center(s) = t_outer(lane, s) (+ line tOffset + sway(s)); mark occupies t_mark_center +- width/2
formulas.notes: outer half lies on next outward lane; for lane 0 position is offset(s)

formulas.name: dash pattern (repeating line)
formulas.expr: visible iff ((s - s_mark - line.sOffset) mod (length+space)) < length, for s >= s_mark + line.sOffset

sections.title: Road marking types and lines (<type>/<line>)
sections.summary: <type> (named, total width) contains one or more <line> elements placed side by side; each line repeats a visible length + gap space pattern along the lane, with its own sOffset, tOffset, width, color and passing rule. More specific than the @type keyword.
concepts: <type width> = sum of line widths plus gaps between them; supersedes roadMark width
line color/width supersede roadMark values
length=visible part, space=gap
tOffset relative to lane border, follows sway

sections.title: Offsets in road markings (<sway>)
sections.summary: <sway> moves the marking's lateral reference away from the lane border by a cubic in ds (relative to roadMark sOffset), so lines can curve independently of the lane, e.g. through construction sites.
concepts: sway applies to the following (explicit) type definition
line tOffset is added on top of sway

formulas.name: sway
formulas.vars: ds measured from sway start (roadMark sOffset + sway@ds)
formulas.notes: restarts each element; final mark t = t_border + sway + line.tOffset

sections.summary: 1.9 allows one permanent and at most one temporary <lanes> layer per road. The temporary layer overlays roadworks lanes and markings with higher priority, links to permanent lanes at its ends, and must not exceed the permanent surface.

sections.title: Annex D (1.8/1.9): smoothness of lanes
sections.summary: Connected drivable lanes must have no horizontal gaps or kinks and no vertical gaps along s, and should have no vertical kinks; touching points (start/end of inner/outer edges with x,y,z,heading,pitch,roll) must match approximately. All lane-section boundaries and road/lane/junction links are critical transitions.
concepts: drivable: driving, entry, exit, onRamp, offRamp, connectingRamp, slipLane, biking(advisory), border, stop, restricted (+deprecated HOV, bidirectional, bus, mwyEntry, mwyExit, roadWorks, taxi)
touching points compare x,y (gap), heading (kink), z/roll (vertical gap), pitch (vertical kink)
no numeric tolerance given
